transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the solvent-cleaning cell ready for Monday morning. We have a mobile exhaust fan available that can be positioned at the cell's temporary duct connection to provide additional capture during the campaign. Before I authorize anything, I need both maintenance and environmental health and safety to review the setup per our Monday-start routine. Can we walk through what's needed to get that review scheduled?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should flag something from my electrical check over the weekend. The mobile fan's startup draw can overload the cell's existing circuit, so it needs to be connected to a dedicated 32-amp breaker with an interlock. Installing that breaker and interlock will take exactly 2 hours. I completed the panel inspection during the weekend shift, so I haven't entered the check in the work-order system yet — we'll need to account for that.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share important findings from my air-monitoring review. The lab uploaded the monitoring sheet after our daily EHS handoff, so I haven't forwarded it yet — but it shows a peak VOC reading of exactly 85 ppm at the cell during door-open cleaning, which is well above our 50 ppm action level. Because of that, the mobile fan must run continuously during the entire solvent-cleaning campaign, and I need to take VOC readings for exactly 4 hours on the first operating shift to confirm capture is adequate. I'll get the monitoring sheet distributed to everyone today.
transcript.speaker: A3
